hook.en: India, Pakistan and China set out on their development journeys within a few years of each other. Why did they end up so far apart?
hook.kn: ಭಾರತ, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ ಮತ್ತು ಚೀನಾ ಕೆಲವೇ ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪಯಣ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದವು. ಅವು ಇಷ್ಟು ದೂರವಾದದ್ದು ಏಕೆ?

objectives.en: Explain why nations compare development with neighbours
Compare the early paths of India, Pakistan and China

narration.en: India, Pakistan and China set out on their development journeys within a few years of each other. Why did they end up so far apart?
narration.kn: ಭಾರತ, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ ಮತ್ತು ಚೀನಾ ಕೆಲವೇ ವರ್ಷಗಳ ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿ ಪಯಣ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದವು. ಅವು ಇಷ್ಟು ದೂರವಾದದ್ದು ಏಕೆ?

body.en: Nations form regional and global groupings such as SAARC, ASEAN, BRICS, G-20 and the European Union to strengthen their economies. It is therefore useful to understand the development paths of our neighbours. India, Pakistan and China have many similarities: India and Pakistan became independent in 1947 and the People's Republic of China was established in 1949. All three started planning in similar ways: India's First Five Year Plan was for 1951–56, Pakistan announced its first plan, now called the Medium Term Development Plan, in 1956, and China announced its first plan in 1953. India and Pakistan adopted similar strategies, such as a large public sector and public spending on social development.

points.en: Regional groupings: SAARC, ASEAN, BRICS, G-20

narration.en: Countries form groups like SAARC and BRICS, so it helps to know our neighbours. India, Pakistan and China all started around the same time and all chose planning: India in 1951, China in 1953 and Pakistan in 1956.
narration.kn: ಸಾರ್ಕ್, ಬ್ರಿಕ್ಸ್‌ನಂತಹ ಗುಂಪುಗಳಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ನೆರೆಯವರನ್ನು ಅರಿಯುವುದು ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ. ಭಾರತ, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ, ಚೀನಾ ಸುಮಾರು ಒಂದೇ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಯೋಜನೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿದವು: ಭಾರತ 1951, ಚೀನಾ 1953, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ 1956.

title.en: On the board: Three neighbours, one starting line

narration.en: Let us draw a timeline of the three neighbours.

say.en: India, Pakistan and China started their development journeys at almost the same time.
India and Pakistan became independent in 1947; the People's Republic of China was set up in 1949.
All three began planning: India in 1951, China in 1953 and Pakistan in 1956.
Reforms came later and in a different order: China in 1978, Pakistan in 1988, India in 1991.
Till the 1980s, their growth rates and per capita incomes were similar. Then their paths split.

prompt.en: Sort each policy or event: did it belong to India, to Pakistan, or to both?
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ನೀತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಘಟನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ: ಭಾರತದ್ದೇ, ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನದ್ದೇ ಅಥವಾ ಎರಡರದ್ದೇ?

text.en: A mixed economy with public and private sectors
Import substitution industrialisation in the 1950s and 1960s
Green Revolution raised food grain output
Capital goods industries nationalised in the 1970s
Denationalisation and a push to the private sector in the late 1970s and 1980s
Heavy reliance on remittances from workers in the Middle East
First Five Year Plan launched in 1951

explanation.en: Both countries began with mixed economies, import substitution and the Green Revolution. Pakistan nationalised in the 1970s, turned to the private sector after that and began reforms in 1988; India planned from 1951 and reformed in 1991.

body.en: Pakistan also followed a mixed economy model with co-existence of the public and private sectors. In the 1950s and 1960s it used a regulated policy framework for import substitution industrialisation, combining tariff protection for consumer goods with direct import controls. The Green Revolution led to mechanisation and more public investment in infrastructure, raising food grain production. In the 1970s capital goods industries were nationalised. In the late 1970s and 1980s policy shifted to denationalisation and encouragement of the private sector; financial support from Western nations and remittances from emigrants to the Middle East helped growth. Reforms were introduced in 1988.

narration.en: Pakistan protected its industries in the 1950s and 1960s, nationalised capital goods industries in the 1970s, then turned to the private sector, helped by remittances from the Middle East. It began reforms in 1988.
narration.kn: ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನ 1950-60ರಲ್ಲಿ ಆಮದು ಪರ್ಯಾಯ ನೀತಿ ಅನುಸರಿಸಿತು, 1970ರಲ್ಲಿ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಸರಕು ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳನ್ನು ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಕರಿಸಿತು, ನಂತರ ಖಾಸಗಿ ವಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಒತ್ತು ನೀಡಿತು. 1988ರಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಧಾರಣೆ ಆರಂಭಿಸಿತು.

problem.en: Arrange these events in time order: China announces its First Five Year Plan; India begins its First Five Year Plan; the People's Republic of China is established; Pakistan announces its first five year plan.

steps.en: India's First Five Year Plan begins: 1951.

answer.en: 1949 PRC → 1951 India's plan → 1953 China's plan → 1956 Pakistan's plan.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Arrange these events in time order: China announces its First Five Year Plan; India begins its First Five Year Plan; the People's Republic of China is established; Pakistan announces its first five year plan.

body.en: Plans: India, China, Pakistan (1951, 1953, 1956). Reforms: China, Pakistan, India (1978, 1988, 1991), the same letters as the Consumer Price Index.

narration.en: Plans go I, C, P. Reforms go C, P, I, like the Consumer Price Index.
